chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Ishaq ibn al-Mubarak said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the Zakat al-Fitr, is it from what Allah said: 'Establish prayer and give zakat'? He said: Yes. And he said: The charity of dates is more beloved to me because my father (peace be upon him) used to give charity in dates. I said: Should its value be made silver and given to one man or two? He said: Distributing it is more beloved to me, and there is no harm in making it silver, and dates are more beloved to me. I said: Should it be given to those other than the Ahl al-Wilayah from these neighbors? He said: Yes, the neighbors are more entitled to it. I said: Should I give the one man three sa' and four sa'? He said: Yes. So this report implies several things: First, that he chose distribution in the state of Taqiyyah (dissimulation) because the belief of all the Sunnis agrees with that, and it does not agree with us regarding the obligation of giving one sa' to one person. Second, that the report does not indicate that it is permissible to distribute one sa', and it is possible that he referred to one who is obligated to provide Fitr for many heads, so distributing it among a group of needy people is better than giving it to one person. Third, that he meant that when the needy are gathered, and there is not enough to distribute the one sa' among them, then distribution is permissible, and perhaps that is the better option.

key_terms.أَصِيُع: Asi' (plural of Sa', a volume measure)
key_terms.أَهْلُ الوَلَايَةِ: Ahl al-Wilayah (people of authority/guidance, often referring to the Imams or their followers)
key_terms.رَأس: Ra's (a unit of measure, specifically one Sa' of food)
key_terms.صَدَقَةِ الفِطرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (charity of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred form of Zakat al-Fitr and can it be given in cash or silver?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while Zakat al-Fitr is rooted in the Quranic command of Zakah, he personally prefers distributing it in kind (dates) as practiced by his father, Imam Ali (AS), though giving its monetary value is permissible. The Imam’s preference for splitting the amount among multiple recipients is interpreted by scholars through three lenses: adherence to the Sunni majority view for *Taqiyyah*, the superior merit of aiding more individuals, or practical necessity when a single recipient cannot consume the entire share. This highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the form and distribution of Fitrah while maintaining its spiritual essence.
